Report the email to IT Security immediately â€” legitimate charity pages never require work credentials
IT Security will investigate whether the internal email account was compromised to send the link
Wait for IT Security's guidance before visiting any links from the same sender
explanation: A donation page requesting work credentials is a credential phishing page. The fact that the link came via an internal email suggests that account was compromised. IT Security must investigate the source and scope of the compromise.

prompt: A general staff member working from home receives a recorded phone message saying their national insurance number has been compromised and they must press 1 to speak to a government agent. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not press 1 or interact with the call in any way
End the call immediately
Report the call to Action Fraud or the relevant national reporting authority
Inform your IT Security team if you received the call on your work phone
explanation: Government impersonation robocalls are a common scam. Pressing 1 connects you to a fraudster who will attempt to extract personal or financial information. Report the call to the appropriate authority and inform IT Security if it reached a work device.

prompt: A remote worker accidentally installs a browser extension that was not on the company approved list, thinking it would help with productivity. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remove the extension from the browser immediately
Report the installation to IT Security â€” unapproved extensions can harvest browsing data
IT Security will assess whether any data was accessed or transmitted by the extension
Only install browser extensions from the company-approved software list in the future
explanation: Unapproved browser extensions can read all data on pages you visit, including credentials and client information. Even well-intentioned installations must be reported so IT Security can assess whether any data was exposed during the time the extension was active.

prompt: A sales team member receives an automated survey from a customer satisfaction tool they do not recognise, which asks them to log in using their work credentials to view client feedback. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not log in using your work credentials
Contact your sales manager to ask whether the survey tool is used by the company
If the tool is not company-approved, report the survey email to IT Security
Access client feedback only through the tools listed in your company's approved software catalogue
explanation: Credential phishing using fake survey or feedback tools is increasingly common. Verifying with your manager and using only approved tools ensures you never enter work credentials into an unauthorised system.

prompt: An employee working from home has their screen visible through a window that faces a shared car park. Neighbours and passers-by can potentially see the screen content. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Reposition the workstation so the screen is not visible through the window
Close the blinds or curtains when working on sensitive content if repositioning is not possible
Use a privacy screen filter as an additional safeguard
Report to your manager if you believe sensitive data may have been observed before the issue was resolved
explanation: Home working environments must meet the same confidentiality standards as the office. Screens visible from outside present a real risk of data exposure. Physical repositioning, window coverings, and privacy filters are all appropriate controls.

prompt: An operations supervisor is told by a team member that they gave their site access code to a colleague because the colleague forgot theirs. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remind the team member that access codes are personal and must never be shared
Report the code-sharing incident to physical security so the code can be changed
The team member who forgot their code should be reminded to use the proper procedure for code resets
Document the incident and issue a reminder to all team members about access code security
explanation: Shared access codes defeat the purpose of individual access control. The code must be changed immediately. Both employees need to understand why sharing is prohibited, and the broader team should receive a timely reminder.

prompt: A general staff member receives an email from the IT team saying their password will remain unchanged as requested â€” but they made no such request. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not ignore the email â€” it may mean someone tried to change your password on your behalf
Call the IT helpdesk immediately on the official number to report that you made no such request
IT Security will investigate whether someone attempted to interact with your account
Change your password from a trusted device once IT Security confirms it is safe to do so
explanation: A confirmation for an action you did not take means someone else may have attempted to change your account settings. IT Security must investigate whether the account is being targeted before you take any further action.

prompt: A sales team member is about to use a public PC at a conference venue to access their company email for an urgent message. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not log in to company accounts on a public or shared PC
Use your work mobile phone or personal hotspot with your work laptop instead
If no alternative is available, use the company's web portal in a private browser window and log out completely immediately after
Report to IT Security that you accessed company email from a public device so they can monitor for unusual account activity
explanation: Public PCs can have keyloggers or browser extensions that capture credentials. Using your own device over a mobile hotspot is far safer. If a public PC is unavoidable, minimise the session, use private browsing, log out fully, and report to IT Security.

prompt: An employee receives a message from their company's HR system saying their personal emergency contact details have been updated. They did not make this change. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not log in using any link in the message
Call HR directly using a known internal number to report the unauthorised change
HR will restore the correct details and refer the matter to IT Security
IT Security will investigate how the change was made and whether your HR account has been accessed by someone else
explanation: An unauthorised change to emergency contact details could indicate someone has accessed the HR system with your credentials. HR must correct the record and IT Security must investigate the account access. The HR portal should only be accessed via the direct URL you know.

prompt: A remote worker receives an email saying a large file has been shared with them via the company's file storage system, but the link goes to a domain they do not recognise rather than the company's usual file sharing platform. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not click the link
Contact the person who apparently sent the share request using a separate channel to verify they sent it
If they did not send it, report the email to IT Security as a phishing attempt
If they did send it, ask them to reshare the file through the company's approved file sharing platform instead
explanation: A shared-file link pointing to an unrecognised domain is a phishing technique that tricks users into entering credentials or downloading harmful files. Verifying directly with the sender removes all doubt, and resharing through the approved platform ensures safety.

prompt: An HR manager is clearing out old physical employee files that contain sensitive personal and financial data. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Separate the sensitive documents from general waste or standard recycling
Place the sensitive documents into a locked, designated confidential waste bin
Ensure the bin is collected only by the approved secure destruction vendor
Obtain and file the certificate of destruction from the vendor for compliance records
explanation: Sensitive HR documents must never go in standard bins. They must be kept secure until destroyed by an approved vendor, and the destruction must be documented for data protection compliance.

prompt: You are sitting at the reception desk when an unknown person rushes past you through the security gates without swiping a badge, claiming they are late for a meeting. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not attempt to physically restrain the person
Alert building security immediately, providing a clear description of the individual and the direction they went
Notify the facilities or office manager so they can alert staff on the floor
Log the incident in the physical security incident register
explanation: Physical safety comes first, so never physically intervene. Security teams are trained to handle breaches. Alerting them immediately allows them to intercept the intruder. Logging the event is required for physical security audits.

prompt: An IT Helpdesk agent receives an urgent call from someone claiming to be the CEO, demanding an immediate MFA reset because they are about to dial into a board meeting. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Apologise for the delay but explain that security protocols require identity verification for all staff, including executives
Use the company's approved verification method, such as calling the CEO's registered mobile number or verifying with their Executive Assistant
If the identity cannot be verified, refuse the MFA reset and report the call to IT Security
If verified successfully, proceed with the reset and log the verification method in the ticket
explanation: Attackers frequently impersonate senior executives to bypass security controls using urgency. Identity verification processes must be followed for everyone without exception. A legitimate executive should expect and respect these controls.

prompt: You enter a meeting room and notice the previous occupants left a whiteboard covered in sensitive financial projections for an upcoming unannounced merger. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Close the meeting room door to prevent others from seeing the whiteboard
Erase the whiteboard completely using the provided cleaning materials
Check the room for any printed documents or notes left behind
Remind the meeting organiser about the clean desk and clear screen policy
explanation: Securing the room and destroying the sensitive information immediately prevents an internal leak. Checking for other left-behind materials ensures nothing else is exposed. A gentle reminder helps reinforce the policy.

prompt: You find a colleague's building access badge lying on the floor in the staff kitchen. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Pick up the badge immediately to prevent anyone else from taking it
Do not try to locate the colleague yourself or leave the badge on their desk
Hand the badge directly to building security or reception
Security will temporarily disable the badge and contact the employee securely to return it
explanation: An unattended badge is a severe physical security risk. Leaving it on a desk leaves it vulnerable. Security must take control of the badge, disable it to prevent misuse in the interim, and verify the identity of the person claiming it.

prompt: An employee is walking into the secure server room, and a contractor they don't recognise tries to follow them through the door before it closes. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Turn and politely ask the contractor to swipe their own access badge
If they do not have a badge or it doesn't work, refuse them entry
Ensure the door closes and locks completely before you continue into the room
Report the tailgating attempt to physical security or the IT manager immediately
explanation: Tailgating is a common method for bypassing physical access controls. Everyone must swipe their own badge to ensure access is logged and authorized. Reporting the incident allows security to investigate the unauthorized individual.

prompt: You notice an individual without a visitor badge wandering alone through the legal department's filing area. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Approach the individual and politely ask if you can help them find someone
Ask who their host or escort is
If they do not have a host or cannot explain their presence, ask them to accompany you back to reception
If they refuse or act aggressively, move away and call building security immediately
explanation: Challenging unescorted strangers in secure areas is a critical security responsibility. Most often they are just lost. However, if they cannot account for their presence, they must be escorted out or handled by professional security.

prompt: A staff member receives an internal mail envelope that has no return address, is unusually heavy, and has strange stains on it. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not open, shake, or smell the envelope
Place it gently on a clear surface and move away from it
Clear the immediate area of other staff members
Call building security or facilities management to report a suspicious package
explanation: Suspicious packages must be handled with extreme care. Opening or moving them can trigger a device or release hazardous materials. Isolating the package and alerting trained personnel is the safest response.

prompt: While in the staff breakroom, you overhear two colleagues loudly discussing the poor performance review of a third colleague who is not present. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Interrupt the conversation politely and mention that they are in a public space
Remind them that performance reviews are confidential HR matters
Suggest they move to a private meeting room if they need to continue the work discussion
If you are a manager, follow up with them later about appropriate handling of sensitive information
explanation: Discussing confidential HR information in public areas is a breach of privacy. Immediate intervention stops the breach from continuing. Reminding them of the policy reinforces good security culture.

prompt: A colleague tells you they forgot their security badge at home and asks to borrow yours just to get through the turnstiles, promising to give it right back. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely refuse to lend your badge
Explain that sharing badges violates company security policy and compromises access logs
Direct the colleague to the reception desk or security office to obtain a temporary visitor or replacement badge
Ensure they do not try to tailgate you or someone else through the turnstile
explanation: Security badges are tied to individual identities for audit and access control purposes. Sharing badges breaks this system. The correct procedure is always to obtain a temporary badge through official channels.

prompt: You see a colleague plug a personal, unauthorized smart speaker into an ethernet port in a conference room to play music. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Ask the colleague to unplug the device from the corporate network immediately
Explain that unauthorized personal devices can introduce vulnerabilities or eavesdrop on conversations
Suggest they use a Bluetooth connection to their phone instead, without connecting to the network
Report the incident to IT Security so they can check for any network anomalies from the device
explanation: Unauthorized IoT devices connected to corporate networks pose significant security risks, including unauthorized data collection and serving as a network backdoor. They must be disconnected immediately and the event reported.

prompt: You find a set of keys left dangling in the lock of a physical filing cabinet marked 'Confidential - Legal'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remove the keys from the lock and lock the cabinet securely
Check the immediate area to see if a member of the legal team is nearby
If no one is there, hand the keys directly to the department manager or building security
Inform them where you found the keys so the incident can be logged
explanation: Leaving keys in a lock defeats the purpose of the physical security control. Securing the cabinet prevents unauthorized access. Handing the keys to an authoritative figure ensures they are returned securely and the lapse is noted.

prompt: You notice an employee from a different department rummaging through your manager's desk while the manager is out for lunch. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Approach the person and ask what they are looking for
If they claim the manager gave them permission, ask them to wait while you call the manager to verify
If you cannot verify or they refuse to wait, ask them to leave the desk area immediately
Report the incident to your manager and HR or Security as a potential internal breach
explanation: Searching another employee's desk without their presence is highly suspicious. Challenging the action and attempting verification is the correct approach. Reporting ensures the manager is aware and can check if anything is missing.

prompt: You sit at a hot-desk and find a sticky note attached to the monitor with a username and password written on it. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not use the credentials to log in to any systems
Take the sticky note and hand it to IT Security or the helpdesk
IT Security will identify the account owner and force an immediate password reset
IT Security will contact the employee to remind them of the password security policy
explanation: Written passwords in plain sight are a major security violation. Leaving it there or throwing it away leaves the account compromised. IT Security must force a reset to secure the account properly.

prompt: An employee notices a cleaner plugging a personal mobile phone into a corporate workstation's USB port to charge it. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely ask the cleaner to unplug the phone from the workstation
Explain that company policy forbids plugging personal devices into corporate computers
Direct them to a standard electrical wall socket for charging instead
Report the observation to IT Security so they can monitor the workstation for any unauthorized data transfer
explanation: USB connections can transfer malware or exfiltrate data, even if just used for charging. Personal devices should never be plugged into corporate endpoints. IT Security needs to verify that no malicious activity occurred.

prompt: You receive a call on your desk phone from someone claiming to be from the IT department, asking you to read out your password so they can fix a background syncing issue. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to provide your password
End the call immediately
Call the official IT helpdesk number to verify if there is a legitimate syncing issue
Report the phone call as a vishing (voice phishing) attempt to IT Security
explanation: Legitimate IT staff will never ask for your password. This is a classic social engineering attack. Refusing, hanging up, and verifying via official channels protects your credentials.

prompt: A person wearing a maintenance uniform asks to use your logged-in computer for 'just two minutes' to check a work order on the internet because their tablet died. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse the request to use your logged-in session
Explain that security policy prohibits letting anyone else use your account
Offer to lock your screen so they can use a guest account if the device allows it, or direct them to a public kiosk or reception
If they become insistent, lock your screen, walk away, and alert building security
explanation: Allowing someone to use your logged-in session means any actions they take (including installing malware or stealing data) will be attributed to you. You are responsible for all activity on your account.

prompt: An HR representative is conducting a termination meeting. The terminated employee becomes angry and refuses to hand over their company laptop and building badge. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not try to physically take the items from the employee
Calmly end the meeting and allow the employee to leave the room
Immediately contact IT Security to remotely lock and wipe the laptop
Contact physical security to deactivate the badge and ensure the employee leaves the building safely
explanation: Physical safety is the highest priority. If an employee refuses to surrender assets, do not escalate the conflict. Rely on logical controls (remote wipe, badge deactivation) to secure the company's data and premises.

prompt: You are walking down the corridor and find a printed spreadsheet containing a list of employee names and their current salaries lying on the floor. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Pick up the document immediately and shield its contents from others
Do not read the details beyond confirming it is sensitive payroll data
Take the document directly to the HR department or your Data Protection Officer
Report where and when you found it so they can investigate the data handling failure
explanation: Unsecured payroll data is a severe internal data breach. The priority is to secure the document immediately to prevent further exposure and hand it over to the appropriate department for investigation.

prompt: An employee notices that the secure disposal bin (confidential waste console) in the finance department is overflowing, and documents are visible and accessible. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not attempt to push the documents down or retrieve them
Inform the facilities management or security team immediately that the bin is compromised
Ask colleagues to temporarily store confidential waste in locked drawers until the bin is cleared
Facilities will arrange an urgent ad-hoc collection from the secure destruction vendor
explanation: An overflowing confidential waste bin is a physical data security risk. Facilities must be notified to arrange immediate collection, and staff must use alternative secure storage to prevent further exposure.

prompt: You are processing an internal transfer. An employee is moving from the Finance team to the Marketing team. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Notify IT and the Finance department manager of the exact transfer date
Ensure IT revokes access to all Finance-specific folders, systems, and distribution lists on the transfer date
Grant the new access required for the Marketing role only after the old access is removed
Conduct an access review a week later to confirm no legacy Finance permissions remain
explanation: Role changes often lead to 'privilege creep' where employees accumulate access they no longer need. Access must be explicitly revoked for the old role to maintain the principle of least privilege.

prompt: A delivery driver arrives at the office suite and asks to drop a large package directly at an employee's desk inside the secure office area. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not allow the delivery driver into the secure office area
Ask the driver to leave the package at the reception or mailroom delivery point
Sign for the package if authorized, or have the receptionist process it
Contact the employee to collect the package from the secure reception area
explanation: Couriers and delivery drivers are unvetted external personnel and must not be allowed into secure office areas where sensitive data or assets are present. All deliveries must be processed at a designated checkpoint.

prompt: A colleague sets up a wireless router in their office because they claim the corporate Wi-Fi is too weak. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Advise the colleague that unauthorized networking equipment is a severe security violation
Ask them to unplug the rogue router immediately
Report the device to IT Security so they can investigate the network exposure
Suggest the colleague log a standard IT support ticket to address the weak Wi-Fi signal
explanation: Rogue access points bypass corporate network security controls, allowing attackers outside the building to connect to the internal network. They must be removed immediately and investigated by IT.

prompt: You find a corporate laptop left unattended and unlocked in the staff canteen. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Lock the computer screen immediately using the keyboard shortcut
Check if the owner is nearby or returning to the table
If the owner cannot be found, take the laptop to IT Security or the local IT helpdesk for safekeeping
IT will secure the device and notify the employee's manager about the policy violation
explanation: An unlocked device is an open door to the corporate network. Locking it secures the immediate threat. If abandoned, handing it to IT ensures it is kept safe and the employee is educated on the risks.

prompt: An administrator receives an email from the HR Director's account asking for a list of all employee home addresses to be emailed to a third-party consultant's Gmail account. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not compile or send the list of addresses
Call the HR Director on their internal phone number to verify the request verbally
If the Director did not make the request, report the email to IT Security as a compromised account or spoofing attempt
If the request is genuine, advise the Director that personal data must be shared via secure, approved channels, not sent to personal email accounts
explanation: Requests to send bulk personal data to unverified external email accounts are highly suspicious, even if they appear to come from an executive. Verbal verification and adherence to secure data transfer policies are mandatory.

prompt: An employee is using the shared office printer and notices the previous user left a USB flash drive plugged into the printer's USB port. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not plug the USB drive into your own computer to see who it belongs to
Remove the USB drive from the printer
Hand the drive to IT Security or the helpdesk
IT Security will examine the drive safely to identify the owner and check for malware
explanation: USB drives found in the office could contain malware or sensitive data. Plugging it into a workstation is dangerous. IT Security has safe environments to examine found media.

prompt: A contractor finishes their 6-month project. On their last day, they pack up their desk to leave. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Collect their physical building access badge and any physical keys
Collect all company-issued hardware, including laptops, phones, and physical tokens
Notify IT to immediately disable their network, email, and VPN access
Remind the contractor of their ongoing non-disclosure and confidentiality obligations
explanation: Offboarding contractors requires strict revocation of both physical and logical access to prevent post-contract unauthorized access. Collecting assets and disabling accounts simultaneously minimizes risk.

prompt: You notice the door to the network communications closet (comm room) has been propped open with a fire extinguisher to keep the room cool. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remove the fire extinguisher and ensure the door closes and locks securely
Check that no unauthorized persons are inside the room
Report the incident to facilities and IT Security
Facilities must investigate the cooling issue so staff do not prop the door open again
explanation: Propping open secure doors compromises physical security and violates fire safety codes. The immediate response is to secure the door, followed by addressing the root cause (cooling) so the behavior isn't repeated.

prompt: A staff member is preparing a presentation on a flight. The person sitting next to them keeps leaning over and reading the screen, which contains unreleased financial results. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Angle your screen away from the passenger and reduce the screen brightness
If they continue looking, close the presentation and stop working on sensitive material
Work on non-confidential tasks for the remainder of the flight
Request a privacy screen filter from IT upon returning to the office for future travel
explanation: Shoulder surfing in public transport is a common way confidential data is leaked. If physical adjustments don't work, the only secure option is to stop processing the sensitive data until in a private environment.

prompt: An employee discovers that a shared departmental folder has broad permissions, allowing anyone in the entire company to read the HR disciplinary templates and records stored inside. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not download, copy, or distribute any of the files in the folder
Immediately report the overly broad permissions to the IT Helpdesk and the folder owner
IT will restrict access to the folder to authorized personnel only
IT Security will audit the access logs to see if unauthorized staff viewed the files
explanation: Over-permissioned folders are a common source of internal data breaches. Reporting it allows IT to fix the permissions immediately, and auditing helps determine the extent of any data exposure.

prompt: During a fire alarm evacuation, an employee grabs a stack of highly confidential legal contracts from their desk to take outside with them. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Keep the documents secure and out of sight while waiting at the assembly point
Do not leave the documents unattended on walls, benches, or in coffee shops during the evacuation
Maintain physical control of the documents at all times
Return the documents securely to the locked office once the building is cleared for re-entry
explanation: Life safety always takes precedence, but if confidential documents are removed during an evacuation, the employee remains responsible for their physical security in the chaotic environment outside.

prompt: You are organizing a department clean-up day. You find several old hard drives in a storage cupboard. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not plug the hard drives into any computer to check what is on them
Gather the hard drives and hand them over to IT Security or the IT asset management team
IT will check the inventory and securely wipe the drives using certified software
If the drives are at the end of their life, IT will arrange physical destruction through an approved vendor
explanation: Old hard drives may contain sensitive legacy data or malware. They must be handled through formal IT asset disposal processes to ensure data is irretrievably destroyed and documented.

prompt: An employee notices a colleague taking photos of their computer screen with a personal smartphone. The screen displays the company's internal customer database. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Note the time and what was visible on the screen
Do not confront the colleague directly, as they may delete the evidence
Report the behavior immediately and confidentially to IT Security and your manager
IT Security and HR will conduct a formal investigation into potential data exfiltration
explanation: Taking photos of screens is a low-tech way to steal data without triggering digital DLP (Data Loss Prevention) alerts. Confronting them ruins the investigation. Prompt, confidential reporting is essential.

prompt: A manager asks an intern to quickly reset the manager's password because the manager is driving and locked out of their account. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse the request to reset or access the manager's account
Explain that sharing credentials or bypassing the self-service reset process violates security policy
Advise the manager to contact the IT Helpdesk directly once they are safely parked
Report the incident to IT if the manager becomes abusive or insists on the violation
explanation: No one, regardless of seniority, can authorize a bypass of credential security policies. Interns and junior staff must feel empowered to refuse insecure requests. Official channels must always be used.

prompt: An executive assistant receives a request from the CEO to wire a large sum of money immediately to secure a vendor contract, bypassing standard procurement protocols due to urgency. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not initiate the wire transfer based solely on the email or message
Call the CEO using a known, verified internal phone number to confirm the request verbally
If confirmed, inform the CEO that company policy requires a secondary authorization from Finance for large transactions
If the request was fraudulent, report the phishing attempt to IT Security immediately
explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) often uses urgency to bypass controls. High-value transactions must always be verified via a secondary, out-of-band channel (like a phone call), and standard financial controls cannot be bypassed.

prompt: You are organizing a team lunch and notice a colleague left a printout of the company's internal IP address schema on the lunchroom table. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Retrieve the document from the table immediately
Check the area to see if the colleague who left it is nearby
If they are not, take the document to IT Security or your manager
Remind the team that technical documentation should not be left in common areas
explanation: Internal network maps are sensitive information that attackers can use for reconnaissance. It must be secured immediately and handed to IT, who will follow up on the policy breach.

prompt: A new starter arrives on their first day, but HR has not yet informed IT. The new starter asks to use your computer to check their personal email while they wait. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely decline the request to use your logged-in computer
Direct the new starter to the HR department or a designated waiting area
Ensure HR formally requests their IT access so accounts can be properly provisioned
Only allow them to use company systems once they have their own secure login credentials
explanation: Sharing a logged-in session, even with a new employee, violates security policy. The new starter must be properly vetted and provisioned with their own accounts before accessing any corporate systems.

prompt: You observe a vendor repairing the office HVAC system. The vendor takes out a USB drive and asks to plug it into an office computer to 'download a manual'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Instruct the vendor not to plug the USB drive into any corporate device
Direct them to use their own mobile device or laptop to access the internet
Report the incident to the facilities manager who is escorting or managing the vendor
If the vendor insists, contact IT Security or building security for assistance
explanation: External media from unvetted third parties is a major malware vector. Vendors must use their own equipment for their tasks. Challenging this action prevents potential infection.

prompt: A manager asks you to bypass the change management process and deploy an urgent code fix to the production server immediately. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Acknowledge the urgency but state that the change management process must be followed
Initiate the emergency change process, which typically requires a rapid review by a designated approver
Deploy the fix only after the emergency change has been formally approved
Ensure all documentation and post-incident reviews are completed afterward
explanation: Bypassing change management leads to undocumented, risky changes that can cause outages or security vulnerabilities. Emergency procedures exist to handle urgent fixes while maintaining an audit trail.

prompt: You receive a physical letter via internal mail marked 'Confidential - Addressee Only', but the envelope is already torn open. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not read the contents of the letter
Place the torn envelope and its contents into a secure, opaque folder or new envelope
Deliver it directly to the intended recipient and inform them it arrived open
Report the incident to the mailroom manager or security so they can investigate potential mail tampering
explanation: Open confidential mail is a security incident. The priority is to protect the privacy of the contents from yourself and others, deliver it securely, and report the tampering.

prompt: An employee notices a security camera in the hallway is pointing downward at a strange angle, covering a blind spot where it shouldn't be focused. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not attempt to adjust the camera yourself
Take a photo or note the exact location of the camera
Report the tampered camera to physical security or the facilities manager
Security will investigate if it was accidentally bumped or intentionally moved to hide unauthorized activity
explanation: Tampered physical security controls are a red flag for impending or past unauthorized activity. They must be reported so trained personnel can investigate and realign the equipment.

prompt: During a desk move, you find an envelope containing physical access cards that belonged to former employees. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Secure the envelope so no one else can take the cards
Deliver the cards immediately to physical security or the HR department
Inform them where you found the cards
Security will verify that the cards have been deactivated and destroy them securely
explanation: Old access cards that haven't been destroyed pose a risk if they weren't properly deactivated in the system. Returning them to security ensures the loop is closed and the physical tokens are destroyed.

prompt: You are presenting a quarterly update in a conference room. You need to connect your laptop to the screen, but you notice a strange dongle attached between the HDMI cable and the wall port. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not connect your laptop to the cable
Leave the dongle exactly where it is
Contact IT Security immediately to report the suspicious hardware
Wait for IT to remove the device and verify the room is safe before proceeding
explanation: Hardware keyloggers or screen-capture devices can be hidden in meeting room cables. Connecting to them exposes your data. They must be handled by IT as forensic evidence.

prompt: A colleague is using their personal tablet to take photos of physical whiteboards containing architecture diagrams after a brainstorming session. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remind the colleague that capturing internal diagrams on personal devices violates company policy
Ask them to delete the photos from their device
Suggest they use a company-issued device to take the photos and save them directly to a secure internal folder
If they refuse, report the incident to the project manager or IT Security
explanation: Personal devices should not hold corporate intellectual property. The data is unmanaged and could be backed up to personal cloud accounts, causing a data leak.

prompt: An employee is processing payroll and needs to leave their desk urgently for a fire drill. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Lock the computer screen immediately
Place any physical payroll documents into a locking drawer or cabinet
Evacuate the building following the standard fire drill procedures
Do not take the confidential documents outside to the assembly point
explanation: During an emergency, life safety is paramount, but securing data takes only seconds (Ctrl+Alt+Del). Leaving sensitive documents exposed during a drill, when many people are moving around, is a major risk.

prompt: A junior developer is asked by a senior developer to share their AWS access keys via Slack so the senior developer can 'fix something quickly'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to share the AWS access keys via Slack or any other method
Explain that sharing credentials violates the principle of individual accountability
Suggest the senior developer request the necessary permissions for their own account via the proper channels
Report the request to the engineering manager if the senior developer applies pressure
explanation: Access keys are equivalent to passwords and must never be shared. The senior developer should have their own access. Sharing keys ruins auditability and creates significant security risks.

prompt: You hear a loud argument in the HR department between an HR manager and a visibly upset employee discussing a grievance. The office door is open. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Move away from the area to ensure you do not overhear sensitive details
Quietly approach the HR manager's office and gently close the door to provide privacy
If the situation sounds physically unsafe, alert building security immediately
Do not discuss what you heard with other colleagues
explanation: Grievance discussions are highly confidential. Providing privacy by closing the door protects the employee's data. Escalating only if there is a physical threat ensures safety without unnecessary gossip.

prompt: A marketing team member wants to use an unapproved, free online tool to convert a PDF containing customer data into an Excel spreadsheet. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Advise the colleague not to upload company data to unapproved third-party websites
Explain that free tools often retain the data uploaded to them, leading to a data breach
Help them find an approved internal tool or software that performs the conversion
If no internal tool exists, request IT to evaluate and provide a secure solution
explanation: Shadow IT, especially free online converters, is a massive data leakage risk. Data must never be uploaded to unvetted external services. IT must provide secure alternatives.

prompt: An employee receives a frantic call from the 'Helpdesk' stating their account is currently being hacked and they need the employee to read out the MFA code they just received to block the attack. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not read the MFA code to the caller
Hang up the phone immediately
Call the official IT Helpdesk number to report the social engineering attempt
Change your account password as the attacker likely already has your credentials and is only missing the MFA code
explanation: Legitimate helpdesks will never ask you to read out an MFA code. If an attacker triggers an MFA prompt, it means they already know your password. You must refuse, report, and change your password.

prompt: You notice the lock on the door to the physical archive room, where paper records of old contracts are kept, has been broken and the door is slightly ajar. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not enter the room or touch the lock
Stand guard near the door to ensure no one else enters
Call physical security or facilities management immediately to report the broken lock
Security will investigate the breach and arrange for an emergency repair of the door
explanation: A broken lock on a secure room is a physical breach. Preserving the scene for security and preventing further unauthorized access are the immediate priorities.

prompt: A colleague asks you to email a sensitive legal document to their personal Gmail account so they can print it at home, as the office printer is broken. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to send the sensitive document to a personal email address
Explain that sending company data outside the corporate network violates data protection policies
Offer to help them fix the office printer or find another working printer in the building
If they need to work on it at home, ensure they access it via the approved corporate VPN on a company device
explanation: Data must remain within corporate boundaries. Personal email accounts are not secure or auditable. The convenience of printing does not override data security requirements.

prompt: You find a mobile phone belonging to a senior executive left in a restroom stall. The phone is unlocked. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Pick up the phone but do not look through any apps, messages, or emails
Press the power button to lock the screen immediately
Take the phone directly to the executive, their assistant, or IT Security
Report where you found it so they are aware it was out of their possession
explanation: An unlocked executive device holds highly sensitive data. Locking it secures the device immediately. Returning it to authorized personnel minimizes the risk of data exposure.

prompt: A member of the finance team receives an invoice from a known vendor, but the email asks them to update the vendor's payment bank details to a new account. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not update the bank details in the finance system based on the email
Look up the vendor's established contact number from the internal vendor database
Call the vendor on the known number to verbally verify the request for a change of bank details
If the vendor denies making the request, report the email to IT Security as invoice fraud
explanation: Invoice fraud often involves spoofed emails requesting bank detail changes. Always verify such requests via an out-of-band communication method using trusted contact information.

prompt: You are closing the office late at night and notice a window on the ground floor has been left wide open. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Close and securely lock the window
Check the immediate area to ensure nothing appears missing or disturbed
Report the open window to building security or the facilities manager before you leave
Security will log the incident and remind staff to secure windows at the end of the day
explanation: Open windows defeat physical security perimeters. Securing it immediately prevents intrusion. Reporting it allows facilities to track security lapses and enforce closing procedures.

prompt: An employee receives a 'password expiry' email with a link, but they are using a Mac and the email references a 'Windows password'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Recognize the discrepancy as a strong indicator of a phishing attempt
Do not click the link or reply to the email
Use the 'Report Phishing' button in the email client to alert IT Security
Delete the email from your inbox
explanation: Generic phishing templates often contain errors that don't match the user's actual environment. Recognizing these discrepancies and reporting them helps IT block the campaign.

prompt: During a system outage, a department manager instructs staff to use a public cloud storage service (like personal Dropbox) to share files until the internal servers are back up. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely push back and explain that using unapproved personal cloud storage is a security risk
Check with IT to see if there is an approved backup collaboration platform or alternative
If no approved alternative exists, delay non-critical work until the systems are restored
Report the manager's instruction to IT Security or the Compliance Officer
explanation: Operational convenience during an outage does not justify breaking security policy. Data placed in unmanaged personal cloud storage is extremely difficult to recover or secure once the outage is over.

prompt: You find a stack of CVs belonging to job applicants left on the printer in a shared hallway. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Retrieve the CVs from the printer immediately
Identify the HR team member responsible for recruitment
Hand the CVs directly to the HR member and remind them to use 'secure print' functionality
If the HR member is unavailable, lock the documents in a secure drawer until they return
explanation: CVs contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and must be protected. Removing them from public areas and returning them to HR mitigates the risk. 'Secure print' (requiring a PIN at the printer) should be used for such documents.

prompt: An employee notices a colleague is recording a video of the office layout and employee desks to post on social media as a 'day in the life' vlog. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Ask the colleague to stop recording immediately
Explain that recording the office layout and computer screens can expose confidential information and compromise physical security
Request that they delete any footage that captures screens, whiteboards, or security controls
Report the incident to the manager or HR, as social media recording usually violates corporate policy
explanation: Office videos can inadvertently leak intellectual property on screens, physical security layouts (like badge readers), and employee PII. Staff must challenge and report unauthorized recording.

prompt: A customer service representative is on a call with a customer who is becoming abusive and demands the representative look up the account details of their ex-spouse. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remain calm and refuse to look up the ex-spouse's account
Explain that data privacy laws prohibit sharing account details without the account holder's direct authorization
If the customer remains abusive, warn them that the call will be terminated
Terminate the call and report the incident to a supervisor
explanation: Social engineering via intimidation is common. Staff must adhere strictly to privacy laws and company policy regarding data access, regardless of a caller's emotional state.

prompt: You are cleaning your desk and find a notebook from a project that concluded three years ago, containing detailed system architecture notes. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not throw the notebook into the regular recycling or trash bin
Check the company's data retention policy for project documentation
If the data is no longer needed, place the notebook in a secure confidential waste console for shredding
If it must be kept, transfer it to a secure, locked physical archive
explanation: Handwritten notes about systems or sensitive projects are just as confidential as digital files. They must be disposed of securely through confidential waste processes to prevent dumpster diving.

prompt: An employee receives a calendar invite from an external vendor, but the meeting location is set to a link that downloads an '.exe' file instead of a standard video conferencing link. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not click the link or download the executable file
Contact the vendor via email or phone to confirm if they intended to send the invite
If the vendor is unaware, report the calendar invite to IT Security as a phishing/malware attempt
Delete the calendar invite from your schedule
explanation: Calendar invites are increasingly used to bypass email filters. An '.exe' file in an invite is highly suspicious and indicative of malware. Verification and reporting are the correct steps.

prompt: A colleague is leaving the company today and asks you to copy a folder of 'useful templates' they created onto their personal USB drive so they can use them at their next job. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to copy the files to the personal USB drive
Explain that company templates and work products are corporate intellectual property
Advise the colleague that transferring data to personal devices upon departure is a policy violation
If they insist or become agitated, inform HR or IT Security
explanation: Data exfiltration by departing employees is a significant risk. Even generic templates belong to the company. Assisting in transferring them is a violation of policy.

prompt: You are testing a new internal application and notice that it displays the full credit card numbers of customers in the test environment, rather than masked data. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Stop testing the application immediately
Take a screenshot (if permitted) or make a note of the exact screen displaying the unmasked data
Report the data exposure immediately to the development team lead and the Compliance Officer
Ensure the defect is logged as a critical security issue that must be fixed before release
explanation: Displaying unmasked credit card data (PAN) violates PCI-DSS compliance, even in test environments. This is a critical security defect that must be addressed immediately by the development team.

prompt: A cleaner is vacuuming the office after hours and unplugs a server rack's UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) to plug in their vacuum cleaner. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: If you witness this, immediately ask the cleaner to stop and plug the UPS back in
Explain that critical IT equipment must never be unplugged
Report the incident to the facilities manager so they can provide proper training to the cleaning staff
Notify IT Operations to ensure the UPS and servers did not suffer an outage
explanation: Physical disruption of power is a threat to system availability. Cleaning staff must be trained on what outlets they can use. Immediate correction and reporting ensure the systems remain online.

prompt: An employee receives an email from HR stating their payroll account is suspended and they must download a PDF form, fill it out with their banking details, and reply. The PDF looks slightly blurry. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not download the PDF attachment
Do not reply to the email with any banking details
Call the HR department directly using a known internal number to verify the request
Forward the email to IT Security for analysis, as it is likely a malicious attachment or phishing attempt
explanation: Malicious attachments disguised as HR forms are common. Blurry logos or poor formatting are red flags. Verification via phone and reporting to IT Security protects both the employee and the company.

prompt: You are walking through the car park and see a laptop bag sitting unattended next to an employee's car. The car is locked and empty. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Pick up the laptop bag to secure it
Take the bag directly to the building security office or reception
Provide security with the license plate number of the car it was found next to
Security will secure the bag and attempt to contact the employee to return it safely
explanation: An unattended laptop bag is at high risk of theft. Securing it and handing it to physical security ensures the corporate asset is protected and the owner can be identified.

prompt: A colleague boasts that they figured out the manager's password because the manager always uses the name of their dog followed by the current year. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Advise the colleague that guessing or using someone else's password is a security violation
Instruct them not to attempt to log in to the manager's account
Report the incident confidentially to IT Security
IT Security will enforce a password reset for the manager and educate them on creating strong, unpredictable passwords
explanation: Predictable passwords are a vulnerability. A colleague attempting to guess them is an insider threat indicator. IT Security must intervene to secure the manager's account and address the colleague's behavior.

prompt: An employee is setting up a new shared printer in the office and decides to leave the administrator password as 'admin' to make it easier for IT to manage. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Access the printer's configuration settings immediately
Change the default administrator password to a strong, unique password
Record the new password securely in the IT department's approved password manager
Configure the printer to require a PIN for secure printing to prevent documents from sitting unattended
explanation: Default passwords on IoT devices like printers are widely known and easily exploited. They must be changed immediately upon installation to secure the device and the network.

prompt: You see a visitor taking photos of the building's main security desk and the turnstiles with their smartphone. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Approach the visitor politely and inform them that photography of security controls is prohibited
Ask them to delete the photos of the security area
Alert the security desk staff so they are aware of the incident
If the visitor is uncooperative or aggressive, step back and let security handle the situation
explanation: Photographing security controls is a common reconnaissance technique used to plan physical breaches. Staff should challenge this behavior politely but firmly, and escalate to security if necessary.

prompt: An employee receives a frantic message on Teams from their manager, asking them to bypass the dual-authorization requirement for a payroll run because the secondary approver is sick. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Acknowledge the urgency but state that the system requires dual authorization for compliance
Do not attempt to bypass the technical control or use another user's credentials
Identify an authorized alternate approver as defined in the payroll policy
Route the approval to the alternate approver to ensure the payroll is processed securely and compliantly
explanation: Dual authorization is a critical control to prevent fraud. It cannot be bypassed due to absence. Policies should define alternate approvers to handle these situations without compromising security.

prompt: You are organizing a filing cabinet in the HR department and find a folder labeled 'Employee Medical Records' sitting on top of the cabinet instead of locked inside. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Take immediate possession of the folder to secure it
Do not open the folder or read any of the medical records
Lock the folder inside the secure filing cabinet
Report the incident to the HR manager so they can remind the team about the secure handling of sensitive health data
explanation: Medical records are highly sensitive personal data. Leaving them unsecured is a privacy violation. Securing them immediately and reporting the lapse ensures the data is protected and processes are reinforced.

prompt: A delivery person arrives with a stack of pizzas for a team lunch and asks you to hold the secure office door open so they can carry the boxes inside. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely decline to hold the door open for the delivery person
Offer to take the pizzas from them at the door while they wait in the lobby
If the order is too large, ask them to wait while you get a colleague to help carry the food
Ensure the secure door closes and locks before returning to the office area
explanation: Delivery personnel must not enter secure office areas. Holding the door for them (tailgating) bypasses security. Taking the delivery at the perimeter maintains the physical security boundary.

prompt: An employee is preparing for a presentation and emails the slide deck, which contains confidential sales targets, to their personal Yahoo email address so they can review it on their iPad at home. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Delete the email from your personal Yahoo account immediately
Delete the email from your work 'Sent' folder
Report the incident to IT Security as a self-reported policy violation
Use approved methods, such as a corporate-managed iPad or secure remote access, to review the presentation at home
explanation: Sending corporate data to personal email accounts is a data exfiltration risk. Self-reporting the mistake and securely deleting the data mitigates the risk, while using approved tools prevents it in the future.

prompt: You notice a colleague in the finance department writing their system password on the whiteboard in their cubicle so they 'don't forget it'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Inform the colleague that writing passwords on whiteboards is a severe security risk
Ask them to erase the password immediately
Suggest they use the company's approved enterprise password manager instead
If they refuse, report the incident to their manager or IT Security
explanation: Passwords written in plain sight compromise the account entirely. Immediate correction is required. Providing a secure alternative (password manager) helps solve the underlying problem of remembering complex passwords.

prompt: An IT administrator receives a request from a department head to grant 'Domain Admin' rights to a junior analyst for a week so they can install some specialized software. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse the request to grant Domain Admin rights to the junior analyst
Explain that granting excessive privileges violates the principle of least privilege
Offer to have an authorized IT staff member install the software for the analyst
Ensure the software itself is vetted and approved by IT Security before installation
explanation: Domain Admin rights grant complete control over the network. They should never be given to non-IT staff for temporary tasks. IT must perform the installation to maintain security and least privilege.

prompt: You are the last person leaving the office for the day. You notice the door to the server room is wide open, and no one is inside. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Look inside the server room briefly to ensure no unauthorized personnel are present
Close the door firmly and ensure the lock engages
Test the door handle to confirm it is securely locked
Send an email or message to the IT Manager or Facilities reporting that the door was found open
explanation: Securing the server room is critical to protect the core IT infrastructure. Closing and testing the lock secures the area, and reporting it ensures management can address the procedural failure.

prompt: A colleague excitedly tells you they found a USB drive in the parking lot and plugged it into their computer, discovering it contains photos of a recent company event. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Instruct the colleague to stop using the computer immediately
Tell them to leave the USB drive plugged in, as removing it might trigger a malicious script
Contact IT Security immediately to report the unauthorized USB device
Wait for IT Security to examine the computer and remove the device safely
explanation: Found USB drives are often used to deploy malware (USB drop attacks). Once plugged in, the device must be handled by IT to prevent further damage and to investigate the extent of any infection.

prompt: An employee receives a phone call from someone claiming to be a researcher conducting a 'workplace satisfaction survey' and asking for the names and email addresses of the employee's team members. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to provide the names or email addresses of your team members
Politely inform the caller that company policy prohibits sharing internal contact information externally
Hang up the phone
Report the call to IT Security or HR as a potential social engineering or reconnaissance attempt
explanation: Information gathering (reconnaissance) is the first step in a targeted attack. Employees must not share organizational structure or contact details with unverified external parties.

prompt: You are walking past a colleague's desk and see their computer screen displaying a website that appears to be hosting inappropriate or explicit content. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not confront the colleague directly or draw attention to the screen
Walk away from the area to avoid observing the content further
Report the observation confidentially to HR or your manager
HR and IT will investigate the browsing history to determine if a policy violation occurred
explanation: Viewing inappropriate content violates acceptable use policies and creates a hostile work environment. Confrontation can escalate the situation. Confidential reporting allows HR and IT to investigate properly.

prompt: A manager is conducting performance reviews in a glass-walled meeting room. They have printed copies of the reviews spread out on the table, visible to anyone walking past. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Knock on the door to get the manager's attention
Politely inform the manager that the documents on the table are visible through the glass
Suggest they turn the documents face down or move them out of the line of sight
The manager should ensure all sensitive documents are concealed from passersby
explanation: Visual data exposure through glass walls is a common privacy breach. A polite intervention helps the manager correct the issue immediately and protects the employees' confidential data.

prompt: An employee receives a calendar invitation for a mandatory 'Security Training' session from an external email address they don't recognize. The invite contains a link to 'register'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not click the registration link in the calendar invite
Do not accept or decline the invitation
Forward the invitation to IT Security for analysis
Delete the invitation from your calendar once IT Security confirms it is a phishing attempt
explanation: Calendar invites are increasingly used for phishing. Official training will always come from internal sources or known, verified training partners. Suspicious invites must be reported and deleted.

prompt: You find a physical key labeled 'Master Key - Server Room' sitting on the reception desk, but the receptionist is not present. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Take possession of the key immediately to secure it
Wait for the receptionist to return or locate a security guard
Hand the key directly to the receptionist or security guard and explain where you found it
Suggest that highly sensitive keys should be kept in a locked key cabinet, not left on desks
explanation: A master key left unattended compromises the entire facility. It must be secured immediately and returned to an authorized person, with a reminder about secure key management.

prompt: A contractor finishes their work for the day and asks an employee to quickly copy a large dataset to the contractor's personal external hard drive so they can 'work on it from home tonight'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse the request to copy data to the contractor's personal drive
Explain that company data must remain on corporate systems and cannot be transferred to unmanaged devices
Advise the contractor to access the data remotely using the approved corporate VPN if they need to work from home
Report the request to the contractor's manager or IT Security
explanation: Transferring corporate data to unmanaged external drives is a massive data leakage risk. Contractors must use approved, secure remote access methods to interact with company data.

prompt: An employee notices that the secure shredding bin in the office has been propped open with a wedge, allowing anyone to reach in and grab documents. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remove the wedge and ensure the lid of the secure shredding bin closes and locks
Check the immediate area to see if anyone is discarding documents
Report the tampered bin to facilities management or security
Facilities should inspect the bin for damage and remind staff not to prop it open
explanation: Propping open a secure shredding bin defeats its purpose and exposes confidential waste to theft. Securing the bin and reporting the tampering restores physical security.

prompt: You receive a Slack message from the 'IT Department' asking you to download a new 'system optimization tool' from a third-party website linked in the message. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not click the link or download the tool
Verify the identity of the sender by checking their profile and looking for official IT communications
If the message is suspicious, report the Slack message to IT Security
Do not install unapproved software from third-party websites, even if requested internally
explanation: Internal messaging platforms can be compromised or spoofed. IT will generally push software via centralized management tools, not ask users to download it from random external sites.

prompt: A team member is working on a confidential project and leaves their notebook on a table in the office cafÃ© while they go to get a coffee. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Stay near the notebook to ensure no one else reads or takes it
Wait for the team member to return with their coffee
Remind the team member that confidential notebooks should never be left unattended in public areas
Suggest they take the notebook with them or secure it in their bag when stepping away
explanation: Physical notes are often overlooked as a security risk. Guarding the notebook prevents exposure, and reminding the colleague reinforces the clean desk policy for physical media.

prompt: An employee discovers that a former colleague's email account is still active and forwarding all incoming emails to a personal Gmail address. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not send any emails to the former colleague's address
Immediately report the active account and forwarding rule to the IT Helpdesk and IT Security
IT will disable the account and remove the forwarding rule
IT Security will investigate what data was forwarded to the personal address
explanation: Active accounts of former employees with external forwarding rules are severe data exfiltration risks. IT must disable the account immediately and investigate the extent of the leak.

prompt: You are at the reception desk and notice a courier trying to read the visitor logbook, which contains the names and companies of everyone who visited that day. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Politely ask the courier to step back from the desk
Close the visitor logbook or move it out of their line of sight
Explain that visitor information is confidential
Suggest to the receptionist that the logbook should be kept closed or replaced with a digital system
explanation: Visitor logbooks contain PII and business intelligence (who is visiting whom). They should not be readable by delivery personnel or other visitors. Securing the book protects this data.

prompt: A manager asks an employee to share their screen during a video call to review a document, but the employee has their personal WhatsApp web client open in the background, displaying private conversations. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Pause for a moment before sharing the screen
Close or minimize the WhatsApp web client and any other non-work applications
Ensure only the document to be reviewed is visible on the screen
Share the specific application window rather than the entire desktop
explanation: Screen sharing can inadvertently expose personal or confidential data. Users should always prepare their screen before sharing and use application-level sharing instead of full desktop sharing when possible.

prompt: An employee receives an email from the CEO asking them to quickly buy $500 worth of iTunes gift cards for a client presentation and send the codes via email. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Recognize the request as a classic gift card scam
Do not purchase any gift cards or reply to the email
Report the email to IT Security using the 'Report Phishing' button
Delete the email from your inbox
explanation: Executives will never ask employees to buy gift cards and email the codes. This is a very common BEC (Business Email Compromise) scam. Reporting it helps IT block the attacker.

prompt: You are working late and notice a cleaning staff member unplugging a network switch in an open office area to plug in a floor polisher. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Ask the cleaner to immediately plug the network switch back in
Explain that network equipment must remain powered on to maintain connectivity for the office
Help them find a standard wall outlet for their floor polisher
Report the incident to facilities so they can instruct cleaning staff on which outlets to use
explanation: Unplugging network equipment causes immediate outages. Staff must intervene to restore power and report the issue so facilities can provide proper training to cleaning contractors.

prompt: An employee finds a printed list of default passwords for the company's network switches pinned to a noticeboard in the IT department. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Remove the list of passwords from the noticeboard immediately
Hand the list directly to the IT Security Manager or Head of IT
Explain where you found the list
IT management should ensure all default passwords are changed and remind staff to use secure password managers
explanation: Displaying infrastructure passwords in plain text, even in the IT department, is a massive security failure. The document must be secured and the passwords changed immediately.

prompt: A colleague asks you to email a spreadsheet containing customer credit card details to a third-party marketing agency. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to email the spreadsheet
Explain that emailing unencrypted credit card details violates PCI-DSS compliance and company policy
Check if the marketing agency is authorized to receive this data and if there is a secure transfer method (like SFTP)
If unsure, consult with the Compliance Officer or IT Security before transferring any data
explanation: Credit card data (PAN) must never be sent via unencrypted email. Doing so violates strict compliance regulations. Authorized, secure channels must always be used for transferring sensitive financial data.

prompt: You notice that the door to the office building's main electrical room is unlocked and slightly open. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not enter the electrical room
Close the door and check if the lock engages
If it does not lock, report the issue immediately to building security or facilities management
Wait near the door until security or facilities arrives to secure the room
explanation: Electrical rooms contain critical infrastructure. Unauthorized access can lead to sabotage or accidental power outages. The room must be secured immediately and the lock repaired.

prompt: An employee receives a text message on their personal phone claiming to be from the company's IT department, asking them to confirm their login ID to 'prevent account suspension'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not reply to the text message or provide your login ID
Do not click any links in the text message
Take a screenshot of the message
Report the smishing (SMS phishing) attempt to IT Security via official email channels
explanation: IT departments rarely use SMS to handle account suspensions. This is a smishing attack aimed at stealing credentials. Do not interact, capture the evidence, and report it.

prompt: You are walking through the HR department and see a monitor displaying a very detailed, sensitive employee disciplinary report, but the desk is empty. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Avert your eyes to avoid reading the sensitive details
If the computer is unlocked, use the keyboard shortcut to lock the screen
Leave a polite note on the desk reminding the employee to lock their screen
If this is a recurring issue, mention it to the HR manager
explanation: Exposed HR data is a privacy violation. Locking the screen secures the data immediately. A polite note helps educate the employee without unnecessary conflict.

prompt: A new software developer asks for a copy of the production database to test their code on their local laptop because 'the test database doesn't have enough data'. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Refuse to provide a copy of the production database
Explain that production data contains real customer PII and cannot be stored on local laptops
Suggest they use a data masking or anonymization tool to generate realistic test data
Report the request to the development manager to ensure the developer understands data handling policies
explanation: Production data must never be copied to unmanaged local environments for testing. This is a major cause of data breaches. Test data must be anonymized or synthetic.

prompt: You observe an employee taking several reams of printer paper and a company laptop and putting them into their car trunk late on a Friday evening. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not confront the employee in the parking lot
Make a note of the date, time, and what items were being loaded into the car
Report the observation to physical security or your manager on Monday morning
Security will check if the employee had authorization to remove company property
explanation: Removing company property after hours is suspicious and could indicate theft. Confrontation can be dangerous. Documenting and reporting allows security to investigate properly.

prompt: An employee receives an email from a known vendor, but the email contains a link to a 'secure document portal' that requires the employee to log in with their Microsoft 365 credentials. Put the response steps in the correct order.
correctSequence: Do not enter your Microsoft 365 credentials into the portal
Check the URL of the portal to see if it matches the vendor's actual domain or Microsoft's official login page
Call the vendor on a known phone number to verify if they sent the document
If unverified, report the email to IT Security as a potential credential harvesting attack
explanation: Entering corporate credentials into third-party portals is dangerous. Phishing sites often mimic secure portals. Verification and reporting protect against credential theft.
